key_insight: Learn a convex, frame-indifferent dissipation potential with a neural network so the resulting constitutive law stays physically well-posed while being inferred from velocity data.
engineering_relevance: This gives a safer way to identify material behavior in continuum mechanics models for complex fluids, especially when only indirect observations are available.
method: Use an input-convex neural network (ICNNE) to represent the dissipation potential.
Enforce convexity, frame-indifference, and evenness in the second strain-rate invariant by design.
Add a penalty to make the potential dissipative at the origin; couple Firedrake and PyTorch for PDE-constrained training.
evidence_signal: The approach was tested on four problems—compressible Navier-Stokes, Herschel-Bulkley flow, Hibler sea-ice rheology, and DEM data—and the learned potentials recovered known physics, generalized to unseen geometries, and remained stable where unstructured methods diverged.
watch_item: The method depends on careful PDE-neural coupling and a penalty-based dissipativity constraint, so training stability and implementation details may still be sensitive.
paper_title: Well-posed by Design: Learning Constitutive Laws from Velocity Data using Convex Neural Network Potentials
